A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical regression study and contain readable main text, equations, and complete Appendices A–C. Content aligns reliably despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical constructions, sample-complexity bounds, and proofs. Neither its main text nor its appendices contain original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical study and adds related-work references. Neither its main text nor its appendices report experiments, simulations, user studies, or empirical data analyses.

M1.justification: The aggregation procedures and median-of-three algorithm in Theorem 3.11 are unchanged. Adding 'finite' before 'interpolator-based aggregation algorithms' on page 5 clarifies an existing property without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training/evaluation tasks. Realizable regression remains the theoretical setting; the newly cited regression research does not add evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline comparisons. The theoretical comparisons with proper learners and general learning algorithms are unchanged; the added citations are related work.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an experimental evaluation protocol. The cutoff loss, independent sampling assumptions, and sample-size conditions in the theoretical analysis are unchanged.

E4.justification: No ablations, empirical robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or case studies are added or removed. The mathematical constructions and supporting analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The probability and expectation bounds are unchanged mathematical guarantees.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries appear in either version. All reported theoretical results remain unchanged, including the O(dγ/n) expected cutoff-loss bound for median-of-three in Theorem 3.11.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, assumptions, theorem statements, derivations, and proofs are unchanged. All 28 appendix pages match in body text and rendered equations after aligning pagination.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions retain the same claims about γ-graph dimension, median-of-three optimality, superiority over proper learning, and limitations of finite interpolating aggregation.

C2.justification: The explanations of the bounds, learning separations, and finite aggregation failure remain the same. The wording refinements introduce no new applicability boundary, mechanism explanation, or limitation.

D1.justification: The technical specifications of the learning procedures are unchanged. No implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware information, or code/data access information are added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Hanneke et al. (2019) and Attias et al. (2024) on regression sample compression, and Attias and Kontorovich (2024) on aggregation fat-shattering dimension. This modestly expands context without revising the central novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 replaces 'a (broader) class' with 'the class of' in the introduction, adds 'finite' on page 5, and adds two related-work sentences. The section organization and remaining narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Added prose moves Definition 3.1's first bullet to the following page, while the expanded bibliography leaves its final reference on an additional page. The overall typesetting is retained; neither version contains figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves scholarly context by acknowledging relevant work on regression compression and aggregation dimensions in Section 2. The small wording refinements improve explicitness, while the main contributions and all appendix proofs remain unchanged, limiting the overall gain.
